Tessa / team / Vellichor,

Apologies for the slight delay — attached is a concise sizing recommendation (redwood_gpu_hedge_matrix.xlsx) and a short SLA proposal PDF. Summary first, details in attachments.

Executive summary (Phase 1, optimistic workload):
- Baseline tokens/sec mapping: based on the supplied histogram and our v2.2 runtime perf curves, a single high-density slab (A100-80G equiv, 64GB) can sustain ~900 TPS for small chat-style prompts at ~P95=320 ms when micro-batching is tuned for 8–12 tokens per request. However, your avg 500-token call maps closer to 110 TPS per slab at P95 ~340 ms (with KV caching disabled).
- Recommended reserved capacity: 3 slabs (A100-80G equiv) dedicated. Rationale: 3 slabs => steady-state sustained ~330 TPS capacity (3 * 110) which covers baseline 40 TPS comfortably and provides ~8x nominal steady-headroom for bursts with autoscaling/burst pool.
- Burst policy: allow short-term burst to shared burst pool sized to add +240 TPS available for 4 minutes (this is a reserved burst pool we recommend pairing with Dedicated). That keeps short spikes (~120 TPS) within margin while preserving dedicated pool for tail-latency consistency.
- Headroom target: we model ~20–30% operational headroom after adding expected quantization/regression buffer. This matches your ask for P99 < 800 ms in common bursts.

Fallback plan: route to v2.0 (quantized) during sustained bursts >4 minutes or when queue depth exceeds threshold. Expected impact: P95 improves slightly (faster model) but quality delta minimal per our evals; P99 under heavy load remains ~750–900 ms depending on burst shape. We include an automatic-prefetch + prefix-caching recommendation to reduce cold-KV warmup penalty (see sheet).

Operational notes:
- Warmup: schedule a 5–10 minute warmup window before business-hours peaks to prefill KV caches and avoid initial tail spikes.
- Batching: configure dynamic batching up to 32 tokens/request with latency guard at 400 ms to preserve P95.
- Observability: enable per-token latency breakdown and a short (48h) high-fidelity trace retention during the first 30 days of production to detect regressions.

Attachments: redwood_gpu_hedge_matrix.xlsx, sla-proposal-vellichor.pdf

If that looks good I can convert into a one-page MAP and a proposed reserved-capacity quote.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
